components.name: Fine-tuned Political DEBATE NLI stance reader
components.computes: Per-release (and per-tweet) stance toward credit-union interests: support, oppose or neutral (sign -1/0/+1).
components.method: mlburnham/Political_DEBATE_base_v1.0 fine-tuned on cu_stance_label_set.csv (552 rows; seed 42; 3 epochs). A Claude rater pre-labelled and human labels override. CPU, about 0.3 s per document. Reported results: 87.2% vs Claude (distillation); about 85% / kappa 0.76 on a member-grouped human-gold test; ft accuracy 0.839 / kappa 0.742 held out; 0.796 on the 760-row gold frame; 0.571 on the adversarial goldeval frame. It is one of five readers in the stacked press stack and the fallback reader in build_media_blend.
assumptions: Policy stance toward CUs is recoverable from text by NLI entailment
DEBATE neutral means the text is not about the bill, not a missed stance
The held-out test sets (87 or 156 rows) are representative
empirical_questions: Does a fine-tuned NLI stance model outperform supervised TF-IDF/SVM on a member-grouped held-out set of this size (83.9% LinearSVC vs 0.757 transformer reported)?
How much of the accuracy is agreement with the LLM pre-labeller rather than with humans?
Does accuracy drop on adversarial and sign-flip targets (CFPB, interchange) as the 0.571 goldeval figure suggests?

components.name: Supervised and stacked stance readers
components.computes: Stacked stance label per tweet or press item from classical and API readers.
components.method: Best classical model: LinearSVC on word+char TF-IDF, 83.9% / macro-F1 0.816 on untouched test (n=87). Khan-style multi-view augmentation was tested and hurt classical models. Supervised tweet stance reached 0.737 CV on 399 golds. Stanceformer is planned, not built.
assumptions: Target-specific labels are needed; sentiment is not stance
The 456/87/217 split is never reshuffled; CV of about 0.90 is inflated and not quoted
empirical_questions: Does target-aware attention (Stanceformer) improve the neutral class over a TF-IDF SVM on this corpus?
Does paired-input augmentation help transformer readers when it hurts classical readers?

components.name: Lexicoder LSD2015 tone intensity
components.computes: Per-release tone intensity = |net| / words from LSD2015 positive, negative and negated counts.
components.method: stringi regex implementation that matches quanteda data_dictionary_LSD2015 counts; negation phrases are stripped first; 9.6 ms per document.
assumptions: Dictionary counts measure how heated a release is (intensity, not direction)
empirical_questions: Does LSD intensity on congressional press releases correlate with human-coded intensity?
Does multiplying stance sign by tone intensity improve prediction of behaviour over stance sign alone?

components.name: press_value aggregate and human-label overlay
components.computes: press_value = stance_sign x LSD intensity per member x category. Human labels overwrite model stance where valid; 497 of 552 labels overlap the corpus.
components.method: run_stage5.R block 3c is placed after the bill override and the Kennedy fix. Overlaid rows are excluded from model-accuracy measurement.
assumptions: Human labels are authoritative
Overlay rows cannot be used to measure DEBATE accuracy
empirical_questions: How much of the member-level press score is driven by human-overlaid rows versus model rows?

components.name: Two-hop stance x valence decomposition with curated registry
components.computes: cu_alignment = stance(speaker->target) x valence(target->credit unions).
components.method: Measured on 400 tweet golds: stance hop 0.915, valence hop 0.689 (the bottleneck). Composing model stance with oracle valence gives 0.872. Valence registry cu_valence_registry.json v2 (11 derived plus 14 seed entries) is derived from Paul's gold judgments; with 5-fold CV the composition reaches 0.782 accuracy / 0.754 F1 vs a flat baseline of 0.677. Auto-registry variants all fell below the flat baseline.
assumptions: Each target has a stable CU valence the owner can judge
Per-target valence is not keyword-automatable (238 distinct targets in 400 tweets)
empirical_questions: Does an explicit two-stage (target stance, then target valence) label schema beat end-to-end CU-alignment labels on held-out data, as TSE-style decoupling predicts?
How stable is a target's CU valence across Congresses?
Does registry coverage, rather than stance accuracy, explain most residual error?

components.name: Bill-sign valence (direction table, prose matcher; override rejected)
components.computes: Stance sign from a tracked bill's known CU direction when a release names the bill.
components.method: cfpb_bill_directions.csv (Reduce +1 / Expand -1) plus the BILLS table in cu_press_release_scraper.R. The named-bill matcher had 93% precision on 187 releases but went 0 good / 3 bad as a blanket override. The DEBATE bill-sign override (12-member anti-CU prior list) dropped held-out accuracy from 0.839 / kappa 0.742 to 0.770 / 0.630 and was disabled 2026-06-30. The naive directional-verb lexicon (after Park, Lee & Cho 2025) gave 3 good / 43 bad sign changes and was rejected. The narrow Kennedy per-release fix is kept.
assumptions: REFUTED: DEBATE neutral means a missed bill stance
REFUTED: directional verb counts over whole text determine valence
Member priors (anti-bank consumer advocates) need a member-level prior, not a lexicon
empirical_questions: Would an aboutness or prominence guard (the bill is the main topic) make a bill-sign override net-positive on held-out gold?
Does a direction-aware lexicon work when restricted to the sentence that names the bill?

components.name: CFPB axis isolation (registry families plus binding policy_force)
components.computes: CFPB stance split into restraint (+1), expansion (-1), institution (0) and general (0) families.
components.method: policy_force is a binding post-meta override in both stacks, and the CATKW router was tightened. CFPB-negative tiers went D 123 -> 98, R 7 -> 0; no-evidence 174 -> 263.
assumptions: CFPB restraint vs expansion is separable by registry families
CFPB-negative tiers were confounded by party (123 D vs 7 R)
empirical_questions: After isolation, is the CFPB-negative tier still predicted by party once bill-level CFPB votes are controlled?
code_refs: fec/stance registry and CATKW router (exact file not named)

components.name: Media blend (press + social) with recency decay
components.computes: raw cell = (1-0.5f) press/p80 + 0.5f social/p80, with f = min(1, nz/15) shrinkage for thin categories.
components.method: Per post: sign x clip(margin, .25, 1.5) x (0.5 if retweet) x 0.5^(age/HL) / n_categories. Half-life is 2.0 years for press and 0.5 years for social. The press-side recency_weight in the R scraper also uses a 2-year half-life with a 2022-01-01 floor. 20 categories via CATKW regex; CROSSPOST_DEDUP is off by default.
assumptions: Stance salience decays exponentially at the stated half-lives
Social posts carry stance comparable to press after p80 scaling
Thin categories (under 15 members with signal) are unreliable
empirical_questions: What half-life best predicts subsequent votes from past statements?
Do social posts add predictive validity over press releases given that many are ghost-written?
Is shrinkage at nz/15 well calibrated?

components.name: Legacy CU press regex stance and graded tone scorer
components.computes: Per release: CU stance via a regex ladder (default support), graded tone via TONE_LEXICON, and member lean, stance and negativity aggregates.
components.method: Ladder: oppose > support cues > neutral bill cues > default support. GRADED_CUTS c(1,2,3.5,5.5,8). Polarity (Wp-Wn)/(Wp+Wn) per Rice & Zorn. Over-flagging recorded: 21 of 32 neutrals were wrongly scored. Superseded for stance on 2026-06-21 and still computed as a comparison column.
assumptions: CU-mention sentences carry the release's CU stance
Default stance is support
empirical_questions: How biased is a default-support regex relative to human gold, by party?

components.name: ACU speaker mode (planned)
components.computes: Treats ACU-authored press (816 rows, 243 members) as ACU-to-member friend or foe labels.
components.method: The NLI hypothesis is branched by speaker_source; keyword extraction was rejected. Validation gate: held-out accuracy >= 0.851, and Marshall/Hawley ACU rows must net negative. Planned 2026-07-01 and blocked on labels.
assumptions: ACU endorsing a member means pro-CU; ACU criticising a member means anti-CU
empirical_questions: Do advocacy-group statements about a member predict that member's subsequent CU votes better than the member's own statements?

components.name: Stance dynamics and neighbour imputation
components.computes: Quarterly (91-day) stance trajectories in seven classes, plus imputation proposals for missing stances from network neighbours.
components.method: Static band = median + MAD over observed-to-observed transitions (floor .05). Imputation needs at least 5 neighbours and |estimate| >= 0.75; 307 proposals; masking validation gives 77% sign agreement. Proposals only; the matrix is not changed. Co-movement was null on the cosponsor and HCoI layers.
assumptions: Stance is locally similar among network neighbours (co-movement test was null)
empirical_questions: Does neighbour-based stance imputation beat a party-only baseline on masked members?
Do stance changes propagate along cosponsor ties over quarters?

components.name: Frame alignment (cross-member duplication rate)
components.computes: Per-category share of near-duplicate text across members, plus party framing chi-square.
components.method: 3-gram shingle Jaccard >= 0.5. Reported duplication: CU Tax 65%, General CU 60%, Defense 12%. It feeds salience intensity (0.5 + alignment).
assumptions: High shingle overlap indicates coordinated messaging
empirical_questions: Does coordinated (duplicated) messaging predict collective cosponsorship on the same bill?

components.name: Fixed ten-band per-category stance ladder
components.computes: Label per member x 18 categories from a signed raw score.
components.method: Bands: >=0.70 Champion/Defender, >=0.35 Ally, >=0.25 Highly Persuadable, >=0.15 Persuadable, >=0.05 Lean Persuadable, >=-0.05 True Neutral, >=-0.15 Lean Skeptic, >=-0.35 Skeptic, >=-0.70 Highly Skeptical, else Opponent; no evidence shows an em dash. Legislation uses a sqrt scale of 2.0 and media a scale of 1.0. Exceptional rounding adds at most +/-0.05. Since 2026-08-03 four domains use signed empirical midrank CDF curves. DOC CONFLICT: MATHEMATICAL_SPECIFICATION.md line 14 describes median+k*IQR cuts.
assumptions: Missing evidence is never imputed as neutral
Signed scores are comparable across members within a category
empirical_questions: Do label boundaries correspond to observable vote-probability thresholds on CU roll calls?
Are curved-domain labels better calibrated to subsequent behaviour than fixed bands?

components.name: Say-do (costly-signal) gate and delivery multiplier
components.computes: Caps Champion/Defender cells to Ally unless corroborated, applies an overall Champion audit cap, and sets a delivery discount on engine targets.
components.method: Cell gate (fail-closed since 742b68aec): path A = authored or original-cosponsored bill in the category; path V = CU-aligned final-passage vote (lean >= 0.5). Path J (committee gatekeeping) was removed; VERIFIED absent from the current moneyball_core.py. Overall gate: at least 6 top cells, 2/3 delivered, and for >=10 direct bills at least 20% advanced (waived at >=20 bills with all top cells delivered). The overall gate is display-only since 391a4a8b5 and fails open. delivery_mult = clip(1 - 0.15 max(0, gap-1), 0.70, 1.00).
assumptions: Sponsorship and final-passage votes are costly signals; committee office is not an action
High-volume introduction with little advancement indicates cheap talk
empirical_questions: Do members whose top labels fail the say-do gate show lower subsequent CU-aligned behaviour than corroborated members with the same rhetoric?
Is the say-do gap associated with lower bill advancement rates (cheap talk vs effectiveness)?

components.name: Overall tier (IMP-weighted aggregate) and Champion crown
components.computes: Overall label = band of the IMP-weighted mean of tier prototypes (Champion 4 ... Opponent -4), with a +/-0.05 nudge. The display Champion is the primacy board top 13.
components.method: Band cutoffs at 3.0, 2.0, 1.0, 0.4, 0.0, -0.3, -0.75, -1.5. IMP weights include Interchange 2.0, NCUA 1.0, Exam 0.75 and Capital 0.25. Unknown cells are excluded.
assumptions: IMP weights reflect relative issue importance (judgment)
Silence does not dilute earned tiers
empirical_questions: Does an importance-weighted overall stance predict votes on the highest-IMP issues better than an unweighted mean?

components.name: Action-based rank honors (rule G ladder)
components.computes: Recognition labels per policy field from accepted actions only.
components.method: Base: signed action sum with role weights 3/2/1, votes 1, and Congress decay 1/0.8/0.64; cutoffs at 5/15/20% of N. Rule G (default since 2026-09-16): a signed rate per service year from 2021-01-03 (years floored 0.5, capped 6), votes 0.4, no decay; positive and negative sub-cohort shares as recorded; True Neutral for zero record.
assumptions: Only accepted actions earn labels; silence earns none
Low rank never implies opposition
empirical_questions: Is rate-per-service-year a fairer predictor of future CU actions than raw cumulative counts for junior members?

components.name: Primacy (CU-purity) tier board
components.computes: Tier 1/2/3 (13/24/48) of members whose legislative acts are most purely CU-focused.
components.method: factor_raw = sum(role_w x act_w) / sum(role_w) with role weights sponsor 1, original 0.5, cosponsor 0.25. Act weights: cu_primary 1, shared .5, other industry .15, offtopic 0, oppose -1; letters 0.6, amendments x0.5; tensor cell overrides. Shrinkage lambda = min(1, credit/15) toward the agenda-weighted baseline, then an uncertainty penalty K = 0.25. Evidence floor cu_primary >= 0.75. diagnostic_v1 (CLASS_DOCK_PRESS_GRADE_ALL, within-chamber) is default since 2026-09-20. Volume-blind by design.
assumptions: CU purity, not volume, defines primacy (owner intent)
Thin portfolios shrink toward the roster mean
empirical_questions: Do high-purity members deliver more enacted CU-aligned provisions than high-volume, low-purity members?
Does shrinkage at anchor 15 produce better out-of-sample rank stability across Congresses?

components.name: Per-area primacy grade (D-031)
components.computes: grade = sum over areas of IMP x (0.80 n_leg + 0.20 n_press), with within-chamber percentiles.
components.method: leg = role-weighted signed acts x (1 + 0.5 tensor) + 0.4 x votes, per service year (clipped 0.5-6). Press = (pos - neg)/items when items >= 5. Role weights 0.40/0.25/0.15.
assumptions: Within-chamber percentiles avoid cross-chamber comparison (D-027)
Press proportion applies uniformly to all areas (no per-item area tags)
empirical_questions: Does per-area grade predict area-specific roll-call alignment?

components.name: Per-industry tier boards, industry-axes tensor and crown law
components.computes: Separate CU, bank, crypto and fintech boards, and an industry tensor tie-break.
components.method: Same desk method per industry. The tensor cell (relevance x valence) is a secondary tie-break, never blended. Crown law: 12-13 Tier-1 champions, and a champion cannot be a threat in another sector.
assumptions: Industries can be scored independently by the same method
Missing tensor cells are not zero
empirical_questions: Do cross-industry champions exist empirically (members aligned with both banks and CUs on contested bills)?

components.name: Cascade activation kernel build_P and partisan edge factors
components.computes: p(u->v) = x/(x+6) with x = w x cpf x edge_mult(v). cpf_diffusion = 1 for same party and 0.4 + 0.6 sqrt(bpf_u bpf_v) across D/R. cpf_pressure = 1.7 co-partisan, 0.5 out-partisan.
components.method: One shared kernel for cascade, coalition, frontier, scenario, priming and route engines. bpf is the bipartisan share (default 0.24). The two physics factors are deliberately never merged.
assumptions: Cross-party contagion flows through bridge-builders
Co-partisan sources persuade more and out-partisan sources less (Furnas/Bakker source alignment)
Saturation constant 6 is a design choice, not estimated
Receiver susceptibility, not sender loudness, governs activation
empirical_questions: Is cross-party cosponsorship diffusion higher between high-bipartisanship pairs as sqrt(bpf_u bpf_v) predicts?
Can the saturation constant be estimated from observed cosponsorship join timing on a member's network?
Is the co-partisan / out-partisan persuasion ratio near 1.7/0.5 = 3.4 in experimental cue studies?

components.name: Competitive independent cascade with common random numbers
components.computes: Expected pro-CU activations in a two-colour first-to-reach race; bystanders turn anti with probability min(0.9, industry$/400000).
components.method: Keyed splitmix64 draws per (iteration, edge), reseeded with 1000003*SEED+it. SEED 7, MC 20 (scenario 40). Seed activation uses a separate 2^62 key range.
assumptions: Independent edge activations given the draws (Bharathi-Kempe-Salek competitive IC)
Industry money mobilizes neutral bystanders
MC = 20 is adequate
empirical_questions: Does the competitive IC model reproduce observed cosponsorship accumulation curves on CU bills?
Does bystander mobilization scale with industry money as min(0.9, $/400k)?

components.name: Contingent seed activation gate
components.computes: gate(n) = max(0.15, seed_prob(n) x SGATE[tier]); committed allies are never gated.
components.method: SGATE ranges from Highly Persuadable 1.00 down to Opponent 0.35, with unknown 0.85. seed_prob comes from the receptivity layer.
assumptions: A lobbied legislator acts only with a stance-graded take-up probability (Chen et al. UAI 2021 contingency-aware seeding)
empirical_questions: Does lobbying contact convert to cosponsorship at rates that decline with prior stance as SGATE assumes?

components.name: Flip / winnability model
components.computes: pflip = a/(a+b), where a = WM pm (c cu+1)/((c cu+1)+HALFF R) + WP nA/mAt and b is the same with industry money and anti neighbours. flip_value = sum tgt x pflip, with tgt = engagement x PERS x (1+0.3 bpf) x delivery_mult.
components.method: Saturating money term on receipts R (floored at $200k; zero imputed to median). nA = pro-neighbour weight x cpf_pressure. WM 0.35, WP 0.65, HALFF 0.10. A comment cites a Volden-Wiseman passage bonus but the code line has none.
assumptions: Money buys access more than votes (Ansolabehere; Hall & Wayman; Kalla & Broockman)
Peer proximity outweighs money
Money saturates relative to receipts
Flip-side competitive LT has no submodularity guarantee (Borodin et al.)
empirical_questions: Does relative CU vs industry money (as a share of receipts) predict roll-call alignment on CU bills after controlling for party and peers?
What is the empirical peer-vs-money weight ratio in cosponsorship decisions?
Is the effect of contributions concave in the contribution-to-receipts ratio?

components.name: Persuadability table PERS
components.computes: Topic target multiplier by stance tier: Champion 0.10 ... Highly Persuadable 0.65 ... Opponent 0.08; no position PERS_NONE 0.45.
components.method: Fixed design table. PERS_NONE was ratified 2026-07-02 at Ally parity. The no-position default drives about 60% of cells (open M5).
assumptions: Persuadability is inverted-U along the stance ladder
Silence equals uncertainty, not enthusiasm
empirical_questions: Is observed stance change after lobbying highest for middle tiers, as the inverted-U table assumes?

components.name: Money response (lean shift) and money-triggered defection
components.computes: shift = MAXSHIFT x (r/(r+HALF)) x pressure_mult, with r = c x amount/receipts; competitor money is multiplied by LOSSFRAME 1.10. Defection moves floor(|shift|/DTHRESH) rungs; Champion and Opponent are immune.
components.method: MAXSHIFT 18 (cut from 40), HALF 0.10, DTHRESH 11.25. Crossing one rung takes roughly a sixth of receipts.
assumptions: Money moves positions little (null vote-buying literature)
Threats weigh more than gifts (loss aversion, elite-attenuated)
empirical_questions: Do large competitor spends precede measurable stance shifts in press or votes?
Is the effective loss/gain asymmetry for legislators near 1.10?

components.name: Linear-threshold priming (cheapest tip)
components.computes: For each target, the cheapest mix of recruiting pro neighbours and money that closes theta - pressure.
components.method: theta = tier threshold (0.6 ... 3.0) + max(0, -lean/120) + 0.25 per Opponent cell. Cross-party cue factor sqrt(bpf_u bpf_v) (Bakker-Lelkes-Malka). Recruit cost = CEDGE x 0.5 / PERS[tier]. Money closes the gap only up to 0.97 pm units.
assumptions: Linear-threshold adoption over summed neighbour pressure
Out-party cues do not persuade
empirical_questions: Do members join CU bills after a threshold share of their close cosponsorship partners has joined?
Are out-party cosponsors' endorsements ineffective at recruiting new cosponsors?

components.name: Salience shock (Noble-Turner going public)
components.computes: Rally, retreat and backfire probabilities per issue, member steps, and a go-public advisory.
components.method: z = min(1, |D-R tier gap|/3); psi = uncertainty; b = min(0.35, 0.05 + 0.10 psi); p = (1-b)(1-z), q = (1-b)z. Rally: co-partisan +1, out-partisan +0.5 if bpf >= 0.30. Retreat: co +1, out -1. Vulnerable members x1.35 x susc_mult. Defensive appeal raises the threshold by (1 + DELTA/2).
assumptions: Co-partisans move more than out-partisans under salience (Noble & Turner 2024)
Backfire grows with policy uncertainty
Electorally vulnerable members respond more
empirical_questions: After a public campaign on a CU issue, do co-partisans of the campaign's champions shift more than out-partisans?
Does polarization of an issue predict whether going public polarizes positions further (retreat regime)?

components.name: Receptivity layer (susceptibility, incentive, prospect domain, seed probability)
components.computes: Per member: susc, susc_mult [0.70, 1.30], edge_mult [0.80, 1.20], pressure_mult = clip(susc x incent x pt, 0.50, 1.60), and seed_prob = clip(0.60 + 0.10 coop + 0.06 breadth + 0.04 visibility, 0.30, 0.90). The rank is not affected.
components.method: Behavioural basis (default): susc = .40 cooperation_v2 + .30 N(affective) - .20 diligence - .10 dominance, blended 0.70/0.30 with persona when n >= 15 cues. Lexical basis: .40A + .30N - .20C - .10E. incent: retiring 0.60, else clip(1 + .30(comp - 0.5), 0.85, 1.15), neutral when COMPET_MULT is on. pt: 1.15 loss domain, 0.92 safe. PERSONA_W 0.30 is kept by owner ruling. Recorded double-count: cooperation_v2 vs bpf rho +0.888.
assumptions: Neuroticism degrades decisions under pressure (Byrne et al. 2015); the A, C and E signs are design priors, not Byrne findings
Final-term members are less responsive (Fouirnaies & Hall)
Members in a live race are in the loss domain and take risks (Linde & Vis 2016)
No N susceptibility signal has been demonstrated (Nokken-Poole drift MISS; H5 null)
empirical_questions: Do higher-susceptibility members change cosponsorship or votes more after lobbying contact (prospective H2)?
Are retiring members less responsive to PAC money in roll-call alignment?
Do members in competitive races take riskier positions on CU issues than safe-seat members?

components.name: Competitiveness multiplier c (COMPET_MULT)
components.computes: c = 1 + 1.0 x exp(-max(lean, 0)/5.0), range (1, 2], where lean = Cook PVI oriented to the member's party. It scales effective dollars on both money legs.
components.method: Matched by Cook incumbent or district, with overrides; unmatched members get 1.0. Default ON since 2026-10-06 (D-104/D-105/D-107/D-108). Real dollars are unchanged.
assumptions: Dollars buy more in competitive seats (reciprocity NOT validated)
AMPLITUDE and SCALE are uncalibrated owner judgment
empirical_questions: Is the marginal effect of PAC contributions on access or alignment larger in competitive seats?
What decay scale in PVI points best fits contribution-effect heterogeneity?
brain_notes: C:/Users/pgoff/Documents/brain/topics/2026-10-05 competitiveness lane (brain ledger D-104, D-105, D-107, D-108)

components.name: Electoral security, leverage and contest/defend plays
components.computes: Security percentile from Ballotpedia Election_Average; leverage = 1 + 0.8(1 - security); play routes contest-primary, contest-general, defend or none.
components.method: Defend value = comp x positive gap vs the cross-party average. Contest route = the larger of the primary and general gaps. Contest plays convert opponents in spread().
assumptions: Ballotpedia electoral average measures security
empirical_questions: Are CU PAC dollars more effective (in later alignment) in members with lower electoral security?

components.name: Scenario runner (what-if)
components.computes: Change in coalition spread and flip value under user money, defection or stance moves, using CRN at MC 40.
components.method: A defection shifts all movable positions by at most 1 fine tier.
assumptions: A defection is a general disposition shift across issues
empirical_questions: When members switch stance on one CU issue, do they shift on other CU issues too?

components.name: Priority anchor, leave-one-out orientation and engagement signal
components.computes: Topic priority = tier anchor (1, 2/3, 1/3, 0) + alpha x IMP-weighted stance on other topics (alpha 0.15 flip / 0.25 coalition); engagement = block-weighted legislative activity; base = max(0, eng + 0.15 x priority).
components.method: Leave-one-topic-out orientation. Fails closed on an incomplete roster.
assumptions: Stance on other CU issues predicts priority on this issue
empirical_questions: Does leave-one-topic-out stance predict stance on the held-out topic?

components.name: Joint CU budget optimizer
components.computes: Allocation of a $2.5M pot in $500 steps maximizing total winnability, with a per-candidate cap PMAX $10k.
components.method: CELF lazy greedy on per-member concave chunks. Modeled conversions rebuild the queue. Exact only in a fixed stance state. Golovin-Krause bound as a diagnostic. Knee at 20% of peak marginal.
assumptions: The objective is separable and concave in CU dollars (checked numerically)
The pot is one PAC's budget (F2 ruling)
empirical_questions: Does the greedy allocation's predicted gain correlate with realized CU-aligned outcomes in funded vs comparable unfunded members?

components.name: Stance money gate (F1)
components.computes: Members with overall tier Skeptic, Highly Skeptical or Opponent get zero money in every allocator.
components.method: Applied before the top-45 shortlist. Fails open for members with no matrix row. Before the gate 10 opposed members were funded $54,500; after it, 19 were gated and none funded.
assumptions: Overall stance should gate money; one topic cell should not
empirical_questions: Do contributions to opposed members change their positions (backing a counter-strategy)?

components.name: Per-topic flip and coalition allocators
components.computes: Per-topic diagnostic allocations: greedy $1k steps on flip gain; coalition water-fill over the top-45 neutral recruits weighted by marginal spread x (1 + 0.8 bpf).
components.method: Budget $2M per topic, cap $50k. Joint vs naive additive spread is reported (non-additivity).
assumptions: Bridge-builders are better seeds
Topic budgets are diagnostic and not summable
empirical_questions: Is coalition spread from multiple seeds sub-additive in observed cosponsorship data?

components.name: Budget frontier with knee and electoral modes
components.computes: Spread vs cumulative seeds per topic; knee where 4 x gain >= peak; contest factor REPFAC 0.6 x lev.
components.method: Lazy greedy up to 60 seeds under CRN.
assumptions: Diminishing marginal returns to seeds
empirical_questions: Where does the empirical marginal return to additional lobbied cosponsors flatten for CU bills?

components.name: Workbook allocator (top-133 from fixed pot)
components.computes: Funds the top 133 of 533 members from a flat $2.0M in proportion to score (uncapped; max about $25.8k).
components.method: A capped variant ($10k cap, top 250) exists only in a backup and was not applied.
assumptions: Score ordering maps to funding priority
empirical_questions: Is proportional-to-score allocation dominated by the greedy optimizer's allocation in predicted and realized winnability?

components.name: Break-even CU spend and ROI floor
components.computes: The CU dollars that restore baseline flip odds against competitor spend (closed form, 'cannot offset' when q >= 1), and member ROI floor values.
components.method: Solves a(CU)/(a(CU) + b(comp)) = pfbase with the saturating money term; ROI floor parity is checked by roi_verify.py.
assumptions: Competitor and CU money enter a share-type ratio
empirical_questions: Are member positions responsive to the ratio of CU to opposing-industry money rather than its level?

components.name: Sponsor-to-target max-product path and chain hold
components.computes: The most reliable recruitment chain from a sponsor to a target, with per-hop $ and probability; chainHold = product of activeP per hop.
components.method: Dijkstra on -log p. activeP(p) = p/(p + (1-p) x ASKM) with ASKM 0.07 (about a 14x odds shift, unestimated). recruitCost(p) = 1000 + 9000(1-p), clamped to $1k-$10k.
assumptions: Cosponsor-kernel edge probabilities proxy ask success
Active asks raise odds by a constant factor (no study pins it)
Money is capped by FEC limits; difficulty shows up in reliability, not dollars
empirical_questions: What is the empirical lift in cosponsorship probability when an existing cosponsor directly asks a colleague versus passive diffusion?
Does the most-reliable path length predict how quickly a target joins?

components.name: Best-sponsor, multi-target tree and budget max-coverage modes
components.computes: Recruitment trees and budget-bounded recruit sets with coverage cov[v] = 1 - prod(1 - p).
components.method: Greedy max coverage (1-1/e) with locality and degree pruning (GCOMB), plus grow() spread with recruitability x log(deg) x proximity.
assumptions: Approximate submodularity on the cosponsor graph
Community structure is exploitable (Porter-Mucha-Newman; Kim-Kunisky)
empirical_questions: Do members recruited through community-local paths join at higher rates than cross-community targets?

components.name: Cosponsor recruitment route finder (Pareto front)
components.computes: Greedy routes from champion seeds with at most K = 5 recruits per recruiter, giving a Pareto front over cost, expected cosponsors and risk.
components.method: Edge cost = CEDGE/max(0.1, p); value = (gain - lambda(1-p))/cost for lambda in {0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4}. Optional MC reach. MOPBD* (Ren et al.) is cited as concept only.
assumptions: Recruiter whip capacity is bounded
Edge activations are independent
empirical_questions: Is whip capacity per recruiter observably bounded (do prolific recruiters' marginal recruits drop off)?

components.name: Staffer closeness route search
components.computes: The least-cost introduction route to staff anchored at a member office. Hop cost = -ln(0.8 x strength) + w x uncertainty; terminal cost includes a member-context modifier (beta 0.15).
components.method: Bidirectional Dijkstra with heuristic 0 (labelled A*) and Yen loopless alternatives. The default route search is one-directional to a virtual sink (staffer_closeness_routes.py:110-138). Ties within 1e-12 relative: fewer steps wins, then lower cost. The office search excludes uncovered staffers and reports the count.
assumptions: The minimum-cost path approximates the most usable introduction
The prestige modifier is a bonus, not access evidence
empirical_questions: Do shorter or cheaper routes correspond to successful real-world introductions in an outreach log?

components.name: Ordered person-overlap routes and employment-routing overlay
components.computes: Routes through dated Politico-reconciled co-work. distance = ceil(1e6 x 128 / strength), with strength = proximity x log2(1 + days/30). Overlay costs: current co-worker 1, historical 3, reported activity 2, filing 5, policy 8.
components.method: Bidirectional Dijkstra on (cost, steps). User-asserted current co-worker hop at cost 1.
assumptions: Log-scaled shared work days proxy relationship strength
Only Politico career-history evidence creates work ties
empirical_questions: Does shared tenure length (log days) predict the likelihood of a successful warm introduction?

components.name: Cosponsorship network construction
components.computes: Member-to-member weighted cosponsor graph: symmetric (mean of reverse duplicates) for cascades and directed (sponsor -> cosponsor) for recruitment.
components.method: R Stage 3: original cosponsor 1.0, regular 0.5, summed per sponsor's bills; igraph centralities with 1/weight distances. Scraper weights: role weight x SUCCESS x 0.8^(119 - congress) / sqrt(C), passed-origin x3 (Sotoudeh-Porter-Krishnagopal). Five NET_CONFIGs (cu published, holistic, holistic_norm, bank_reg, crypto).
assumptions: Cosponsorship is an influence and alignment tie
Original cosponsorship is a stronger tie than plain cosponsorship
Big bills are weaker ties (1/sqrt(C))
empirical_questions: Do success-weighted cosponsorship ties predict future co-voting or joint sponsorship better than raw counts?
Is the 2:1 original-to-plain cosponsor weight supported by differences in later collaboration?

components.name: Bipartisanship (bpf)
components.computes: Per-member cross-party tie share from cosponsorship only (bipartisan.json / 100, default 0.24).
components.method: Restored to cosponsor-only by S2-01 (bf4a703); BP_SRC=aug gives the unratified augmented definition.
assumptions: Cosponsorship alone measures cross-party bridging
empirical_questions: Does bpf predict cross-party cosponsor recruitment success?

components.name: Social and press-engagement layers
components.computes: Directed edge probabilities from reposts (w 1.0) and mentions (0.4), Fink author-volume normalized (floor 25 posts, pair cap 0.25). Kernel-inverse weight w = 6p/(1-p), cap 2.0; reinforcement x(1 + 0.3 min(1, p/0.10)). Press-title engagement uses ENG_MIN_ITEMS 5.
components.method: Precision-first name matching.
assumptions: Reposts and mentions indicate relational ties (Fink et al. 2023)
empirical_questions: Do Twitter interaction ties predict cosponsorship ties beyond party and state?

components.name: Press HCoI communities
components.computes: Eight Louvain communities over recency-weighted press-category profiles (Pearson >= 0.6, seed 7); topic-affinity edges <= 0.12 for cosponsor-isolated members.
components.method: Hellinger genealogy across time. Homophily replication at press resolution was null.
assumptions: Shared issue attention indicates coalition (Malaterre & Lareau 2024)
empirical_questions: Do press-attention communities predict cosponsorship within community above chance?

components.name: Co-appearance and signed member-reference layers (display only)
components.computes: Pairs who both appeared substantively in the same interview episode (>= 4 turns or >= 200 words; 1,151 pairs). Signed directed references with LLM valence per context window (4,358 edges; green above +0.15, red below -0.15).
components.method: Episodes with more than 8 members are skipped. Edges need at least 2 scored contexts. Name resolution never guesses.
assumptions: Appearing in the same episode indicates a relation
LLM valence of references measures relation sign
empirical_questions: Do negatively signed references predict lower future cosponsorship between the pair?

components.name: Signed-network coalition partition
components.computes: Coalitions from a signed backbone with frustration-minimizing local search seeded by positive Louvain.
components.method: R backbone sdsm (alpha .05, signed). DW-NOMINATE vote edges were rejected in favour of the signed backbone.
assumptions: Signed-network partitioning reveals hidden coalitions (Aref & Neal)
empirical_questions: Do signed-partition coalitions predict joint voting on CU roll calls better than party?

components.name: Press-lean coalition detection (Ward) and bloc profiles
components.computes: Ward.D2 clusters on member lean profiles (9 blocs) and a combined bloc index.
components.method: COALITION_LEAN_WEIGHT 3.0, min 6 members. Static snapshot. All blocs are labelled pro-CU (a known mislabel).
assumptions: Similar press lean profiles form coalitions
empirical_questions: Are press-lean clusters stable across time windows?

components.name: Sector network configurations
components.computes: Bank-regulation and crypto cosponsor graphs alongside the CU graph.
components.method: Hub concentration flag at hub degree >= 3x the second highest. Recorded: bank_reg 4,742 dyads, 76.1% novel vs CU; crypto p_max 0.23 vs CU 0.52 (below the engine floor).
assumptions: Sector bill universes define sector-specific influence networks
empirical_questions: Do sector networks differ in centralization in ways that predict bill passage rates?

components.name: Katz-Bonacich benchmark (diagnostic)
components.computes: Katz-Bonacich centrality on the live kernel (delta = 0.85 / lambda_max), Spearman-correlated with allocations, money and legislative score.
components.method: Power iteration. Not consumed by the chain.
assumptions: Equilibrium contributions are proportional to Katz-Bonacich centrality (Battaglini & Patacchini)
empirical_questions: Do observed PAC contributions to members correlate with Katz-Bonacich centrality in the cosponsor network?

components.name: Concurrent-service OVERLAP edge rule
components.computes: A person-person edge exists only if two people share a container and their payroll intervals intersect.
components.method: Weight = guaranteed overlap x container proximity kappa (personal office 1.00, committee same side 0.75, unknown 0.60, opposite 0.40, leadership 0.75, admin 0.50). 16.0M of 31.1M candidate pairs rejected for zero overlap. After admin exclusion (v6) 4.66M guaranteed pairs remain. Admin containers carried 70.8% of pairs; degree vs largest office size r = 0.87.
assumptions: Concurrent service in a container indicates a real connection
Sequence is a career trajectory, not a tie
Very large containers are suspected catch-all buckets
empirical_questions: Do co-tenured staffers later appear together in lobbying registrations or office moves more than non-overlapping peers?
How much of staffer degree is explained by container size alone?

components.name: Co-tenure weight and workplace exposure index
components.computes: Co-tenure weight = kappa x tier x (1 - exp(-days/365.24)) x shared-role attenuation (0.05). Exposure = sum over workplaces of kappa x alloc_i x alloc_j x integral of 1/max(1, n-1) concurrent headcount; strength = 1 - exp(-exposure/TAU).
components.method: Equal allocation across concurrent workplaces; headcount census of observed people. Shared factors: House 0.02, Senate 0.05.
assumptions: Shared days indicate contact opportunity with diminishing returns
Larger offices dilute pairwise contact (1/n)
empirical_questions: Does inverse-headcount weighting improve prediction of later co-movement between offices?

components.name: Layer-balanced PageRank, eigenvector and bridging diversity
components.computes: PageRank (d = 0.85; sensitivity 0.70 and 0.95) on a walk splitting mass equally across active layers, with group-balanced teleport. Per-component eigenvector (diagnostic). Bridging = normalized Simpson diversity of walk mass across target kinds.
components.method: Duplicate support is collapsed by max. No composite influence score.
assumptions: Equal walk mass per layer is a modeling prior
Values are descriptive, with no causal direction
empirical_questions: Does layer-balanced PageRank rank staffers who later become senior staff or lobbyists higher than degree does?

components.name: Staff directory matching and identity consolidation
components.computes: Quorum staffer to office matches, and automatic duplicate-person merges.
components.method: A never-guess name ladder (nicknames, accents, surname + chamber uniqueness). A payroll-evidence pin plus record-pair title threshold >= 8 characters (raised from 6; the removals were bare 'counsel'). The web-reference loop has made 0 automatic merges. Exact-name candidates feed only an exploratory layer.
assumptions: Payroll account identity with a corroborating record pair means the same person
Short title matches are false matches
empirical_questions: What is the precision and recall of the matching ladder against a hand-labelled sample?

components.name: Recency and access-uncertainty factor
components.computes: cost = 0.35 + ln2 x years since overlap / 5 + 0.25 x workplace concentration; factor = exp(-cost). Not a probability.
components.method: Exposure-weighted last overlap per joint run.
assumptions: Relationship usability decays with a 5-year half-life
empirical_questions: What is the empirical half-life of former co-worker ties as measured by later joint activity?

components.name: Noisy-OR evidence combination and outreach ranking
components.computes: Evidence strength = 1 - prod over sources of (1 - max source strength). Outreach candidates are ordered by PageRank, then route cost.
components.method: Noisy-OR is defined but not in the build path.
assumptions: Distinct source systems are independent evidence
empirical_questions: Are evidence sources for the same staffer tie actually independent (error correlation)?

components.name: Lexical Big Five (Ramey-style closed vocabulary)
components.computes: Corpus-relative Big Five z (O, C, E, A, ES; N = -ES) from category rates of floor speech and interviews.
components.method: Rates per 1000 words (LIWC-analog, Empath, MATTR, Brysbaert concreteness) are z-scored and combined with linear weights from published correlates or SMOreg (Mairesse) fit on essays, then refit to RKH targets per trait (hybrid). Shrinkage z x sqrt(tokens/1500). Held-out CV vs RKH: E .510, A .406, C .363, ES .258, O .214 (mean .350). O was reversed on the party check.
assumptions: Closed-vocabulary rates carry trait signal
RKH estimates are a valid reference (method-shared, so convergence is inflated)
Scores are meaningful only within this corpus
empirical_questions: Do text-derived traits converge with expert or insider ratings of the same legislators (Personality on the Hill)?
Is convergence with RKH inflated by shared method (Mairesse-LIWC on both sides)?
Do traits generalize across genres (floor vs interview vs social)?

components.name: Big Five validation against Senate gold panels and criteria
components.computes: Pass or miss of trait validity looks. E and A pass both panels; O passes academics only; N passes insiders only; C has an insider association only.
components.method: Pre-registered looks: interview C vs votes cast rho +0.155 PASS; C vs follow-through +0.112 PASS. Several improvement rounds MISSed. A-ES about .44 is population-real (RKH benchmark) plus about .21 text-tone halo. Status labels must accompany any external claim.
assumptions: Gold panels are independent ratings
k=1 insider ratings are noisy
empirical_questions: Does text-measured conscientiousness predict roll-call participation and bill follow-through out of sample?
Is the A-ES correlation in text a halo artifact or a population feature?

components.name: LLM item-level reader (Pink), ridge hybrid and CT-CM latent model
components.computes: De-identified, chunked LLM ratings on 20 items; ridge hybrid on lexical, interaction and persona features; CT-CM SEM with an LLM method factor.
components.method: The LLM reader removes names before scoring and codes 'cannot tell' as 0. It is display-only. Pink x behavioural diagonal mean +0.064 < 0.12 fails. CT-CM is a one-look capstone.
assumptions: De-identification removes reputational priors (Cao & Kosinski)
Judge halo is a single method factor
empirical_questions: Do de-identified LLM trait ratings converge with gold panels above lexical methods?
How much of the LLM trait variance is a single halo factor?

components.name: Behavioural dispositions
components.computes: Cooperation, diligence (roll-call participation, LEP), dominance (turn statistics, leadership), visibility (interviews), breadth (portfolio) and reactivity (interview cutoff).
components.method: z-score composites with coverage floors; missing values are neutral.
assumptions: Observed behaviour indicates disposition
Turn-share statistics index dominance (Rienks & Heylen; Valente)
empirical_questions: Do behavioural dispositions predict lobbying responsiveness better than text traits (prospective H1/H2)?

components.name: Cooperation v2 (share-based bridging)
components.computes: Mean of within-chamber z of cross-party tie share and directional cross-party cosponsorship share (at least 10 cosponsorships). Reciprocity is reported only.
components.method: Volume-free by design. Promoted 2026-07-10. Correlates rho .888 with bpf.
assumptions: Cross-party share measures cooperation independent of volume
empirical_questions: Is cross-party cosponsorship share stable across Congresses (trait-like)?

components.name: Affective neuroticism slot and N genre-transfer tests
components.computes: affective_n = z(LIWC i + negemo - posemo) + z(LLM pessimism, anxiety, depression, volatility), residualized on E and party.
components.method: Gate 5/5 passed: |r(N,E)| .039; party .000; LIWC-LLM convergence +.236; split-half SB .742. Promoted 2026-07-11. Genre transfer of interview N to floor and hearing text FAILED (rho .050, .161).
assumptions: Negative-emotion and first-person-singular words track N (Pennebaker)
No gold N criterion exists, so the gate tests construct integrity only
empirical_questions: Does interview-derived affective N transfer to other speech genres?
Does affective N predict yielding under pressure (Byrne mechanism) in observed behaviour?

components.name: Agency/communion persona channel
components.computes: persona_z = 0.60 z(communion) - 0.40 z(agency) from LLM few-shot cue classification (strong 1.0, weak 0.5), blended at PERSONA_W 0.30.
components.method: Functional gate 18/18. Party signature: communion D .099 vs R .049. Persona homophily is not earned (|r| <= 0.015).
assumptions: Projected persona is what a lobbyist meets
Communal rhetoric signals approachability
empirical_questions: Do communal-persona members accept more meetings or cosponsor more with outside requesters?

components.name: Interview weighting (C_INT_W) and gated shrinkage (P6)
components.computes: Conscientiousness aggregates interview chunks at 2x. Members with fewer than 8 measurements are shrunk.
components.method: The P6 reliability claim (.748 -> .831) was retracted as double-shrink inflation; the change was kept on external criterion gains.
assumptions: Shrinkage is judged only on external criteria, not split-half reliability
empirical_questions: Does shrinkage of thin-corpus members improve correlation with external criteria?

components.name: Caption-based speaker verification
components.computes: Per clip: SOLO, MULTI or NOT_SPEAKING, and MATCH, MISMATCH or NONE identity, from auto-captions with Haiku 4.5. Keep = SOLO and not MISMATCH.
components.method: Hard identity cues only. About 33.7% of keeps rest on weak evidence. 2,192 clips, 1,761 kept.
assumptions: Hard cues in captions identify the speaker
empirical_questions: What is the false-accept rate of caption-cue verification against a hand-checked sample?

components.name: eGeMAPS prosody and Whisper disfluency rates
components.computes: 88 eGeMAPS features per clip; member descriptors (pause, pace, volume, strain, pitch); hesitation rate per 1,000 words via prompted faster-whisper.
components.method: ICC and Spearman-Brown reliability: pause .92 > pace .86 > volume .85. Venue confound: live about 26 per 1k vs NPR 0.22 per 1k. The audio-prosody N pilot MISSed at N=90.
assumptions: Vocal features carry stable between-member signal
Sex confounds pitch variability (r = -.266)
empirical_questions: Are disfluency rates stable within member across venues once editing is controlled?
Does prosody carry trait information beyond text (Salam et al. benchmark)?

components.name: Acoustic speaker-ID (closed) and two-check identity design (proposed)
components.computes: Closed: cosine and neural speaker ID (EER .226-.317, failed). Proposed: forced alignment AND ECAPA-TDNN verification, fail-closed, with witness-turn negative controls.
components.method: Pilot bars: EER <= 5%. Awaits rulings D1-D12. Production is blocked at 0 profiles.
assumptions: Speaker embeddings separate members at EER <= 5%
empirical_questions: Can ECAPA-TDNN verification reach EER <= 5% on congressional hearing audio with three enrollment clips?

components.name: congress.gov legislative activity score with Congress decay
components.computes: Per member x 17 sections x 3 roles: bill counts, average cosponsors and success rate, with counts decayed by 0.8^age per Congress (138 columns).
components.method: Role swap on search URLs. Success comes from status text with a fallback classifier. The sentinel ledger also applies 0.8^(119-c) and keeps the strongest role per bill.
assumptions: Recent Congresses matter more by a constant factor
Search terms capture CU-relevant legislation
empirical_questions: Does a 0.8 per-Congress decay maximize prediction of current-Congress CU activity from past activity?

components.name: Ballotpedia committee, caucus and party-leadership scores
components.computes: Committee leadership (Chair 1.0 ... Member 0.2), caucus leadership, party leadership (Speaker 1.0 ... Minority Whip 0.2) and a weighted electoral average (2018 x2).
components.method: Bioguide-keyed (this fixed a five-Johnsons bug). Sub Layer AW:BA is normalized by x/max.
assumptions: Leadership positions indicate CU leverage (hand-set constants)
empirical_questions: Does party leadership rank predict effectiveness on CU bills?

components.name: Signal-prioritized press collection cap
components.computes: Per-member URL cap (default 1000) prioritized by CU-term titles.
components.method: Coverage 86.6% before fixes. P(CU-relevant | CU-term title) = 0.825 vs 0.0089 for generic titles. Coverage: D 92.5% vs R 87%; Senate 83% vs House 96%.
assumptions: CU-term titles proxy CU relevance; missing pages carry about 10% CU signal
empirical_questions: Does differential coverage by party or chamber bias the press pillar?

components.name: Release category taxonomy and billstatus synthetic rows
components.computes: 19 Layer-2 categories under 7 groups via regex, net and count per member; synthetic 'X (co)sponsored' rows from BILLSTATUS XML.
components.method: Billstatus rows were removed from Stage 5 on 2026-06-30; 110 members then had no real releases.
assumptions: Regex terms identify a release's topic
Cosponsorship is a press-layer signal (later rejected)
empirical_questions: What is the precision of regex topic tagging against human coding?

components.name: Five-stage legislative effectiveness shadow and CEL criterion
components.computes: Role-weighted, timing-decayed credit per stage (BILL, AIC, ABC, PASS, LAW), normalized N/5 per chamber-term, decayed 0.8 per Congress. Results-only and 70/30 advocacy composite percentiles. Ceremonial-share criterion against CEL LES.
components.method: Role weights 3/2/1; cosponsor timing 2^(-delay/180); impact weights 1/5/10. A shadow candidate, not activated.
assumptions: Stage progression measures effectiveness (Volden-Wiseman)
Earlier cosponsorship is worth more
More conscientious members sponsor fewer ceremonial bills (RKH)
empirical_questions: Does the shadow score converge with published CEL LES for the same members and Congresses?
Does cosponsor timing (early joiners) predict bill advancement?

components.name: LDA finance-client classification and report join
components.computes: Bank, credit union or other classification with HIGH/LOW confidence. Joined finance reports: 322,473 issue-coded reports; ABA $228M vs CUNA $93M.
components.method: Name regex with guards. NAICS is linkage metadata only. Fail-closed guards. Vintage 2024-10-25; coverage reliable through 2021.
assumptions: Client names are decisive for finance classification
empirical_questions: How does name-based classification compare with Kim et al. positions-based industry assignment?

components.name: Lobbying member-year network and circular lobbied-member link
components.computes: client x bioguide x year dyads (63,991 member-years). Edges are the sponsor and cosponsors of lobbied bills.
components.method: P(joined | lobbied) = 1 by construction, so it is REFUTED as evidence of influence. LD-2 filings never name members.
assumptions: The bill-roster join is not a lobbying-contact measure
empirical_questions: Using an independent contact measure, does lobbying precede cosponsorship more than chance?

components.name: FEC to LDA bridge test
components.computes: Relation between FEC giving and LDA lobbying network change.
components.method: Round 1 VOID. Round 2 p = .098 (Spearman +0.259, N = 52). Round 3: raw rho +0.153, but the four-control partial is -0.0002. Closed pending a new vintage. FEC as a 42-month leading indicator is a candidate heuristic.
assumptions: FEC giving leads lobbying (unvalidated)
empirical_questions: Does industry FEC giving lead LDA lobbying expenditure after controlling for firm size and sector?

components.name: Contact inference (activity to member)
components.computes: Matches lobbying activity descriptions to members.
components.method: Gold positives name the member. Negatives come from the same organisation's roster join, split 50/50 by organisation. Contamination is estimated by a recall sample.
assumptions: Roster-join negatives are not contacts
empirical_questions: What is the precision of description-based contact inference against blind labels?

components.name: Ridge-logistic cosponsor forecaster
components.computes: Predicted cosponsor joins on open bills. A frozen forecast of 265,396 predictions is unscored.
components.method: Ridge logistic regression. Scoring against the lobbied-member table would be circular.
assumptions: Network and lobbying features predict joins
empirical_questions: Does the forecaster beat a cosponsorship-history baseline (Brandenberger reciprocity; Russo et al.)?

components.name: Contested-bills registry
components.computes: Per-bill mode (standard, advisory or contested) adding a counterparty term (Romero Moreno 2021).
components.method: Loader shipped; engine wiring not built.
assumptions: Owner ratification is the only admission route
empirical_questions: On bills where banks and CUs oppose each other, does relative lobbying spend predict outcome?

components.name: Demographic Potential v2.1 (growth room)
components.computes: 0-100 score = 100 x sum(weight x percentile) over LQ strength 20, competitive shift 20, aligned sectors 15, branch whitespace 15, deposit whitespace 5, LMI 10, large employer 8, small business 7.
components.method: LQ = local share / US share; shift-share identity. Qualification LQ >= 1.25. Non-default.
assumptions: Judgmental weights, not estimated
Whitespace is opportunity
empirical_questions: Does growth-room score predict subsequent CU membership or branch growth in a district?

components.name: Demographic Potential v3.0 (CU footprint, default)
components.computes: Score from CU employment LQ .30, establishment LQ .20, branch share .25 and deposit share .25; qualifies at employment LQ >= 1.0.
components.method: Default since 2026-09-16 (D-035). Opposite direction to v2.1.
assumptions: Current footprint is the potential (owner ruling)
empirical_questions: Is a district's CU footprint associated with its members' CU-aligned behaviour (constituency interest)?

components.name: Census congressional-district metrics
components.computes: 489 rows x 25 ACS and CBP metrics at state and district level.
components.method: Census API pulls stacked across levels. Documented boundary mismatch: ACS on 119th-Congress districts, CBP on 116th.
assumptions: Mixed-vintage boundaries are acceptable
empirical_questions: How large is measurement error from the CBP-ACS boundary mismatch for redistricted states?

components.name: Single-look holdout discipline and look ledger
components.computes: Pass or miss of pre-registered confirmatory looks.
components.method: The gate is pre-registered with hashes; a look is consumed once and never re-run; look fragments are void. A joint-null simulation gives about 1.5-2% false pass.
assumptions: Pre-registration prevents basis-shopping
empirical_questions: What is the empirical false-discovery rate of this protocol across the look ledger?

components.name: Gold-set validation and zero-rank-delta gate
components.computes: Trust scores against owner-ruled gold sets, and a byte-identical ranks_python.json check for behaviour-preserving changes.
components.method: Gold sets: 400 tweets, 760 press rows, Senate panels. Freshness: warn after 7 days, fail after 14.
assumptions: Gold labels are independent of the pipeline
empirical_questions: How much do gold-set accuracies differ from accuracy on randomly sampled live rows?

components.name: Prospective receptivity contract (H1/H2) and forecast ledger
components.computes: H1: Spearman(seed_prob, new cosponsorship). H2: Spearman(pressure_mult, |tier movement|). Frozen cosponsor-join and dyad-persistence (p = 0.82) forecasts with Brier scores.
components.method: Bars: >= .20 PASS, .10-.20 DIRECTIONAL, <= -.10 INDICTED. Needs at least 60 days and 150 movers. One look per contract.
assumptions: Cross-sectional Spearman is a valid test
empirical_questions: Does seed_prob predict which members add CU cosponsorships after the freeze date?
Does pressure_mult predict stance movement?

components.name: Receptivity sensitivity harness, MC stability and F5 power gate
components.computes: Top-20/50 target overlap under constant sweeps; seed-set stability across MC budgets; H1/H2 power (requires at least 150 new-event members).
components.method: ROBUST at top-20 overlap >= 18. The F5 replay found 72 of 511 new-event members (UNDERPOWERED; look unspent).
assumptions: A robust target set means the constant cannot change a decision
empirical_questions: Which receptivity constants change targeting decisions, and are those the ones with weakest literature support?

components.name: Employer-string roster matching and overrides
components.computes: Assigns Schedule A rows to roster companies by normalized employer key, prefix tokens and context; override rules use maximum-specificity matching.
components.method: Strict-names rule (roster plus verified aliases only). Acronym collisions are open owner calls.
assumptions: Employer text identifies the employer
Unlisted spellings are unmatched
empirical_questions: What precision and recall does employer-string matching achieve against a hand-coded sample, by company size?

components.name: Contributor identity match ladder
components.computes: AUTO, HIGH, REVIEW or DISCARD for same-name candidates by name parts, zip, city, state, occupation and employer contradiction.
components.method: Ordered rules (exact name + zip -> AUTO, etc.). No name-frequency weighting.
assumptions: Same name + zip implies the same person
empirical_questions: How does rule-based identity matching compare with probabilistic record linkage (frequency-weighted) on FEC donors?

components.name: Receipt-role classification and contradiction-only exclusion
components.computes: Economic role per receipt from form, line and description. A row is excluded only when its own text names another organisation; ambiguous rows are kept with a flag.
components.method: The Banking run excluded 29,816 rows ($32.5M), of which $29.3M came from one prefix bug (CITIZENS read as CITI). Frozen code (2026-09-27).
assumptions: Form/line plus text identify the role
Ambiguity is not contradiction (D-040)
empirical_questions: What share of excluded rows are true misattributions on manual audit?

components.name: Conduit legs, memo dedup, filing-version identity and transfer rule
components.computes: Conduit legs are counted; memo legs are deduped by tuple; one winning amendment version per transaction; 24G/24K transfers; PAS2 index v6 count_latest.
components.method: Known defect: an off-by-cents memo parent ($176,942.05 Crypto double count).
assumptions: Same amount or date means the same transaction version
empirical_questions: How often do FEC amendments change amounts versus dates, and does count_latest bias totals?

components.name: PAC cash proportional attribution
components.computes: A company's share of each PAC payment = its share of labelled cash just before the payment.
components.method: Ordered events, cent-level conservation, withhold on unresolved inputs. The first application failed the cash gate.
assumptions: Cash is fungible within a committee
Same-day receipts come before payments
empirical_questions: How sensitive are attributed totals to the same-day ordering assumption and to FIFO vs proportional rules?

components.name: PAC transfer graph and beneficiary direction partition
components.computes: PAC -> PAC -> candidate flows, and support/oppose/party four-bucket attribution (Dem/Rep = downstream - oppose).
components.method: 89% of beneficiary dollars were oppose. The attributed-estimate producer is unbuilt.
assumptions: Direction codes identify support vs oppose
empirical_questions: What share of industry super-PAC money ultimately supports versus opposes candidates by party?

components.name: Collection completeness (zero provenance, count reconciliation, key pool)
components.computes: Verified zeros, count reconciliation, and pagination-shortfall rejection; key rotation with an hourly budget.
components.method: Only the browser lane stamps zero_verified. Three reconcile passes. The per-key vs per-IP rate limit is unverified.
assumptions: The FEC count is the completeness target
empirical_questions: How often do openFEC recordsTotal values misreport (false zeros) relative to bulk files?

components.name: Cycle-aware giving refit (phase and drift log models, 50/50 growth)
components.computes: Projected measures as log models of presidential vs midterm phase, trajectory and inflation. Growth = 50% prior cycle + 50% IBISWorld budget with a one-year lag.
components.method: Live bundle refit-20261007. Presidential uplift +9% (D-119). Lobbying uses a log refit.
assumptions: Giving depends on election-cycle phase (D-092)
Industry budget is a growth reference (D-113)
empirical_questions: Is industry PAC giving systematically higher in presidential cycles than in the preceding midterm, net of inflation?
Does industry revenue growth improve giving forecasts over a seasonal-naive baseline?

components.name: Slope (R0/R1/R2) and anchor auto-pick
components.computes: Pooled, own or DerSimonian-Laird partially pooled slopes per industry. The same-phase anchor is used only when it wins by 5% in both backtests.
components.method: Own slopes beat the blend (LOEO 10.8 vs 14.3).
assumptions: The rule that wins both backtest designs generalizes
empirical_questions: Does partial pooling of industry slopes reduce forecast error in small-sample sectors?

components.name: Calculator rules, company-PAC nowcast and BLEND
components.computes: Relative change on previous-cycle anchors. Company-PAC nowcast = O + (1-s) B, with s = geometric mean of pace shares. The BLEND (D-099) is overridden by the panel nowcast (D-116). CU cohort of 16 PACs.
components.method: Anchors exclude non-giving receipts. Lobbying is shown in-house vs outside, never summed.
assumptions: Within-cycle pace is informative
empirical_questions: At what month in the cycle does a pace nowcast beat the model forecast?

components.name: Refit gates G0-G9
components.computes: FAIL, HOLD or PUBLISH. G6: no industry's leave-one-election-out MAE may exceed the calculator's. G9 warns when the refit fails to beat naive.
components.method: Waivers applied. Log lobbying MAE 4.050 vs naive 3.936.
assumptions: LOEO MAE is an acceptable criterion
empirical_questions: Do refits that pass G6 forecast the next cycle better than the published calculator?

components.name: PAC-to-candidate accuracy attempts (rolling three-cycle cap)
components.computes: Scored ORIGIN and nowcast forecasts, 2018-2024. Bar: A >= 90 overall and >= 75 per phase.
components.method: v6: ORIGIN B1 plus N/(N+1) cross-sector pace shrinkage. Only telecom passes. A common 2022 drop defeats window rules (DE-066/067).
assumptions: Gains must come from method, not more history
empirical_questions: Was the 2022 drop in industry PAC-to-candidate giving a common shock across sectors?

components.name: Insights seasonal-naive baseline and remainder fix
components.computes: Repeat the same-phase prior cycle; withhold without 4 complete cycles. Conditional additive remainder replaces subtraction (7 of 19 shares had gone negative).
components.method: Seasonal naive.
assumptions: Four-year electoral periodicity
empirical_questions: Does seasonal naive beat growth-augmented models out of sample (3.63 vs 3.99 MAE reported)?

components.name: Sector growth vs giving, partisan share and lobbying regressions
components.computes: log giving ~ sector FE + growth(t-1, t) + phase + tossup + trend; RShare ~ growth + Shift (P - RMajNow); log lobbying with an AR term.
components.method: Wild sector-cluster bootstrap with Holm adjustment; two-way cluster SE as sensitivity; FD sensitivity. Results: no stable partisan shift (-0.04, p .76); the lobbying lead flips sign under year FE; growth adds no adjusted R2.
assumptions: Lagged growth predicts giving
Expected control is known at the time (retrospective for 2023/2025)
empirical_questions: Does sector growth predict political giving after year fixed effects?
Does expected change in party control shift industry partisan giving share?

components.name: SEATS-W weekly seat-gain test (2022 House)
components.computes: Weekly D share of giving vs expected D seats gained: -3.47 pp per seat (House), block-bootstrap p .0086-.0174; Senate null.
components.method: Fixed-X block bootstrap (3 and 5 weeks), Holm; HAC as secondary. One election.
assumptions: As-of seat forecasts precede spending
empirical_questions: Do corporate donors shift partisan giving toward the expected winner as forecasts move within a cycle (strategic access-seeking)?

components.name: CUA (Credit Union Alignment) index
components.computes: Expected weighted exposure over 16 fields in 4 themes (credit .40; digital, auto/insurance, housing .20 each); midrank percentile standing.
components.method: Expected values over class probabilities (PR2), never argmax. Grade D if measured share <= 1/2.
assumptions: Vendor consumer fields measure exposure to ACU issues
Council weights are unratified
empirical_questions: Does CUA standing predict actual CU membership or responsiveness to CU canvassing?

components.name: Participation Index
components.computes: Four themes at 1/4 each over ten sai_* turnout and engagement scores; code 50 on digital reachability is left unscored.
components.method: Weighted index with midrank standing.
assumptions: Vendor propensities are valid
empirical_questions: Do vendor turnout scores predict validated turnout?

components.name: Sphere of Influence
components.computes: 0.45 giving + 0.45 volunteering + 0.10 household; midrank percentile.
components.method: Ratified 2026-10-01 (owner 'leaning').
assumptions: Givers and volunteers engage members of Congress
empirical_questions: Do volunteers and donors contact representatives at higher rates (civic voluntarism)?

components.name: Partisan lean (descriptive, never weighted)
components.computes: Signed lean from registration (0.5) and vendor partisan fields; bands at +/-25 and +/-75; Undetermined when band confidence < 0.80.
components.method: Excluded from the overall score.
assumptions: Registration and vendor codes lie on one axis
empirical_questions: How well do vendor partisan scores agree with registration and primary ballot choice?

components.name: Overall standing (district weights)
components.computes: Colorado: 0.40 CUA + 0.35 Participation + 0.25 Sphere. Candidate districts: 30 CUA / 25 support / 25 participation / 20 sphere. Re-ranked by midrank.
components.method: Fixed linear weights (PR1; approved 2026-10-07).
assumptions: Standings are commensurable
empirical_questions: Does overall standing rank people by realized advocacy action (contacts, turnout)?

components.name: Expected-value cells and uncertainty draws (C0, C3)
components.computes: Monte Carlo redraws of 26 estimated fields (independent C0, household-correlated C3); summed P(top10); analytic SD assuming independence.
assumptions: Imputation probabilities are calibrated
Cells are independent (C3 probes this)
empirical_questions: Are imputation class probabilities calibrated on holdout (ECE)?

components.name: Ridit transforms and rule cells
components.computes: Ridit = (mass below + half mass at code)/N. Children rule D5a. Ordinal maps for owner, homeowner and dwelling.
components.method: Bross ridit.
assumptions: Ordinal order is supported; spacing is arbitrary
empirical_questions: Does ridit scoring change rankings materially versus equal-interval coding?

components.name: Area aggregation with empirical-Bayes shrinkage
components.computes: Beta-binomial EB-shrunk top-decile share per area (block -> tract -> file) using a design effect; area standing and bands.
components.method: Summed probabilities, not flags. Households use the mean of member percentiles. Suppression is superseded in the app (nothing withheld).
assumptions: Areas are exchangeable within the parent
empirical_questions: Does EB shrinkage improve stability of area rankings across file vintages?

components.name: Luna stratified RF/KNN completion
components.computes: Per-field calibrated class probabilities for blank sci_* values; most probable class fills the blank.
components.method: StratifiedGroupKFold by household; RF (128 trees) vs KNN grid; logistic calibration; promotion gate on A2. Colorado holdout 86.67-86.76%. Per-district refits: OR-05 86.64% vs 77.89% majority; CT-01 87.39% vs 77.91%.
assumptions: Missing at random given predictors
No untouched labels remain in Colorado
empirical_questions: Is missingness in vendor consumer fields MAR given observed fields?
Does a model trained on one district transfer to another?

components.name: Prior-corrected rare-class repair
components.computes: Rare-class probability under balanced weights x training prevalence, renormalized.
components.method: Applied to two fields.
assumptions: Balanced weights inflate rare classes by about inverse prevalence
empirical_questions: Does prior correction improve calibration of rare classes on holdout?

components.name: Household model
components.computes: RF with leave-one-out household co-member labels: +1.009 pp holdout (95% +0.959 to +1.060). The shuffled-household control removes the gain.
components.method: Published as section 29.
assumptions: Household members share characteristics
empirical_questions: How much predictive information do household co-members carry for consumer attributes?

components.name: GPU XGBoost round and fill-status rules
components.computes: XGBoost or RF500 fills in 8 fields (+0.087 pp on second holdout use). Majority-default status when lift < 0.5 pp. Historical household copy.
components.method: Section 30 is current. Bigger models gained only about +0.1 pp, so the ceiling is the information in the data.
assumptions: Lift over majority tests the information content of a field
empirical_questions: Is imputation accuracy capped by data information rather than model capacity?

components.name: Candidate support score s
components.computes: Equal-weight average of oriented partisan score, presidential support, registration and recent primary ballot (0-100).
components.method: Missing signals drop out of the denominator. Primary mode awaits a spec.
assumptions: Vendor scores and registration point toward party
empirical_questions: How well does a composite of vendor partisanship and registration predict candidate vote choice (validated against survey or precinct returns)?

components.name: Chance of voting t with PAV calibration
components.computes: Raw t = mean of five turnout scores / 100, then a weighted PAV monotone curve per district fitted to own general-election records. OR mean 0.58 -> 0.83; CT 0.48 -> 0.74.
components.method: Ranking unchanged. Refused below 1000 people.
assumptions: The past general record is the target
Turnout is monotone in score
empirical_questions: Are vendor turnout scores well calibrated to actual turnout, and does isotonic calibration on past records predict future turnout?

components.name: Untapped potential
components.computes: potential = (wp (1 - |2s-1|) t + (1-wp) s (1-t)) x (1 + wi x i), where i = sphere percentile / 100. Knocked doors are excluded.
components.method: VERIFIED in untapped.py:9-10: the supporter weight is tied to 1 - wp, not a separate wR as the brain note describes. Defaults wp 0.5, wi 0.5.
assumptions: Persuasion value peaks at s = 0.5 among likely voters
Mobilization value is in supporters unlikely to vote
empirical_questions: Do canvass contacts move vote choice more among undecided likely voters than among partisans (persuasion RCT heterogeneity)?
Is get-out-the-vote contact most effective among low-to-middle propensity supporters?

components.name: Street-plan presets, turf planner and walk routing
components.computes: Block value per 100 m (mixed-support, supporter turnout or identification). The turf grows along connected streets to 60 doors (400 m jump). Dijkstra routing on the noded TIGER network.
components.method: Blocks need at least 5 doors; length floored at 50 m.
assumptions: Value per walking distance is the efficiency criterion
empirical_questions: Does contacts-per-hour rise with value-per-100 m turf construction relative to precinct-order lists?
